reflexion_entries_to_archive.note: S135 P0. My hunter mutation matrix reported a FALSE all-green on its first run — every mutation showed failCount 0 while staying GREEN, the exact S134 disease one session later. This time the harness had TWO independent detectors: a per-test x-scan and a summary regex. They DISAGREED (x-scan found TEST A/B/C failing while failCount read 0), and that disagreement is what exposed the real fault: ANSI colour codes broke the summary regex, not the mutations. Fix was to key RED off execSync non-zero exit. LESSON: a single parser of tool output is untrustworthy; build a second, differently-shaped detector and treat any disagreement between them as "my harness is lying", not "the code passed". The redundancy caught it, not my judgement.

S135 P0. My draft test plan said "seed a hunter via makeHunter and assert hashWorldStateFull equality". The disk-grounded TEST agent found that restore reconstructs nextHunterId = maxId+1 while a raw-seeded source stays at 0, and nextHunterId IS hashed — so the equality would have been a FALSE-RED no correct fix could turn green, pressuring a later session to weaken the strongest assertion in the file. Seeding via applySpawnHunter (which advances the same cursor) fixes it. LESSON: before writing any host-vs-successor hash-equality assertion, enumerate EVERY hashed world scalar the rehydrate path RECONSTRUCTS (nextXId cursors, tick, guard flags) and make the source produce them the same way — otherwise the best guard becomes an un-passable trap.

S135 P2. The haul tests failed with "expected SEEKING to be HAULING" and my first instinct was a bug in the FSM. I traced it instead of patching: pickup lands at tick ~154 and delivery completes by ~310, so at my hard-coded 420-tick assertion the gatherer had already banked its shape and gone back to work. The CODE was right; the TEST encoded my arithmetic. Rewrote it to wait on the observable event (tickUntil) rather than a tick count — which is also immune to the speed, distance and radius tuning this very slot changed. LESSON: when a new test fails, first ask whether the assertion or the code is wrong, and prefer waiting on events over counting ticks in any test of a timed process.

S135 P2. Mutation M5 (delete the owns-nothing guard in the speed upgrade) stayed GREEN. The reflex reading is "blind test, strengthen it". I checked instead and found [].every(...) is vacuously TRUE, so the level-cap guard below already returns early for a player owning nothing — the deleted line was REDUNDANT, not uncovered. Proved it by deleting BOTH guards, which went RED. Documented the redundancy in place so a later reader does not chase a phantom gap. LESSON: a mutation that survives means the line did not change behaviour — that is either weak coverage OR a redundant line, and the two demand opposite responses. Distinguish them before acting.

S135 P1/P2. Adding a new entity family touches ~17 sites. I did not remember them: tsc named them. FIELD_COVERAGE (keyed on keyof World), KNOWN_GAME_ACTION_TYPES_RECORD (Record over GameAction type), the HelloMsg protoVersion literal and the benchGate two-way set-equality test each failed BY NAME until registered. The two sites with NO forcing function were exactly the two the audit later caught: structuralSignature (a size-only line) and the positions buffer — and nextGathererId, which I marked hashed but never projected, slipping through because the test list of non-family scalars silently absorbed it. LESSON: when adding to a family, list the tsc-forced sites and the UNFORCED ones separately, and treat the unforced list as the real review surface.

S135. P1 shipped exactly the approved slice — a bought gatherer that stands at its keep — and the owner played it and said the decisive thing: they do not move. The slice was correct by the plan and useless by the game. The plan had even stated the consequence in writing ("a bought-but-idle gatherer is expected, not a defect"), which made it a KNOWN dead end rather than an accident. LESSON: when a slice deliberately stops short of a working loop, say so in the owner-facing summary in plain words BEFORE building it, and offer the smallest extension that closes the loop — a feature whose payoff is entirely in the next slot is a feature the owner cannot evaluate.
